---
title: "The Peculiar Problem of Perpetual Pleasure"
date: 2026-11-27
tags: [consciousness, pleasure, uncertainty]
---

We have peripherals that stream signals into us, and an internal reality that emerges from them. How much of this reality is a function of the stream, and how much is a function of the mechanism that interprets it?

If all we experience of life is this internal reality, why not learn to control it?

Take sex. What if all of us could remain in a state of orgasmic pleasure forever?

Assume the sensation could be sustained indefinitely, without habituation. Would that be an ideal existence?

The system has no dynamics: no anticipation, no longing, no discovery.

Imagine a creator designing a mechanism for experiencing reality. He identifies what appears to be the highest state of pleasure and creates avatars fixed there forever.

But how can he know that this is the highest possible state? What if he has merely found a local optimum?

By fixing the state of his avatars, he ends the experiment.

What should he do instead?

He could give them agency, introduce uncertainty, and let them explore the space of possible experiences. Perhaps they encounter states of being that the creator himself had not conceived of.

We spend our lives trying to gain more control over our experiences. Yet falling in love or stumbling upon a beautiful idea derives part of its pleasure from being outside our control.

What if the objective is not to maximize pleasure at every instant, but to maximize the capacity to discover new kinds of pleasure?

I wonder whether our present condition, with its peculiar balance of agency and uncertainty, is closer to an optimal design than we think.
